titulo: One Ordinary Workday in Seven Small Frictions
caption:
One Ordinary Workday in Seven Small Frictions

Cella is a small black rectangle with a crown, and she spends one ordinary workday, from 8:05 a.m. to 5:50 p.m., in seven small frictions. YouTube long video, 16:9. No Short and no Reel in this package.
descripcion:
NAOS. Choose friction.

One ordinary workday, hour by hour, in seven small frictions: a good morning before the laptop opens, the ask in the first minute, the question that gets swallowed, the ok that means no, a yes said in a corridor, the last line of a call, and a note for tomorrow. Cella goes through the seven, what each one costs, and a fix that takes a sentence or two. Where there is a study it goes on the record; the rest is Cella's opinion. For whoever is carrying one small silence into tomorrow.

0:00 One ordinary workday
0:47 8:05 · Good morning
2:08 9:30 · The first minute
3:28 11:10 · The question
4:47 12:40 · The ok
5:41 2:15 · The favor
6:35 4:30 · The last line
7:13 5:50 · The note
8:16 The day, checked

What the research says (so you can check us):
Epley N, Schroeder J. (2014). Mistakenly seeking solitude. Journal of Experimental Psychology: General, 143(5), 1980-1999. https://doi.org/10.1037/a0037323
Flynn FJ, Lake VKB. (2008). If you need help, just ask: Underestimating compliance with direct requests for help. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 95(1), 128-143. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.95.1.128
Huang K, Yeomans M, Brooks AW, Minson J, Gino F. (2017). It doesn't hurt to ask: Question-asking increases liking. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 113(3), 430-452. https://doi.org/10.1037/pspi0000097
Masicampo EJ, Baumeister RF. (2011). Consider it done! Plan making can eliminate the cognitive effects of unfulfilled goals. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 101(4), 667-683. https://doi.org/10.1037/a0024192

The voice describes each study narrowly: commuters told to talk to a stranger reported a more positive ride, and a hint is all that carries over to colleagues; people underestimated by as much as half how likely others were to agree to a direct request for help; people who asked more questions, follow-ups above all, were better liked by their partners in new conversations; and unfinished goals kept intruding on thoughts during unrelated tasks until a specific plan was written.

#selfawareness #workday #NAOS
alt: A 9-minute video in 16:9 about one ordinary workday in seven small frictions. Cella, a small blocky black figure with two round white eyes and a crown, stands in colored rooms while on-screen cards give the hour and the moment: 8:05 a.m. good morning, 9:30 the first minute, 11:10 the question, 12:40 the ok, 2:15 the favor, 4:30 the last line and 5:50 the note. Each part shows what the moment costs, and ends with a three-row card with the small fix and a one-line verdict. Four studies appear with an ON THE RECORD stamp: Epley and Schroeder 2014, Flynn and Lake 2008, Huang and colleagues 2017 and Masicampo and Baumeister 2011; the rest carries a CELLA'S OPINION stamp or is plain opinion. In the last part a 45-second clock runs while the viewer is asked to write down which of the seven happens most. It ends on For whoever is carrying one small silence into tomorrow, and Choose friction. The thumbnail shows Cella large with a crown on an amber field, the words One ordinary workday, and a big 7 on a card.
